items.title: Streaming payouts per stream
items.claim: Reported per-stream payouts from Spotify to rights holders in the early 2020s are roughly which range?
items.reveal_title: Fractions of a cent per stream
items.reveal:
Industry reports and Spotify's Loud and Clear site indicate average per-stream rates of about $0.003 to $0.005, with substantial variation between rights holders and territories.

From 2024 Spotify required tracks to reach 1,000 streams in 12 months before generating royalties at all.
items.why: The economics of recorded music differ fundamentally between physical and streaming eras.

items.title: When A=440 became standard
items.claim: A=440 Hz is the modern reference tuning. When was it widely standardised internationally?
items.reveal_title: Standard pitch was agreed only in the 20th century
items.reveal:
An international conference in London in May 1939 recommended A=440 Hz; ISO 16:1955 confirmed it.

Historical performance practice often uses A=415 Hz (Baroque) or other regional standards.
items.why: Absolute pitch references are conventions that have shifted across centuries.

items.title: How long the Beatles recorded
items.claim: From the first EMI recording session to the band's official break-up, roughly how long did the Beatles record together?
items.reveal_title: About 8 years from first session to break-up
items.reveal:
First EMI session: 6 June 1962. Paul McCartney's public departure announcement: 10 April 1970. Twelve UK studio albums in that period.

George Martin produced almost all of them at Abbey Road.
items.why: Cultural impact and recording duration are not the same thing.
